content:
The real cost of an incomplete RFQ is my own time.

I used to send RFQs that were incomplete. I thought it was a minor issue. It was not.

I would spend 14 hours a month chasing my own packages. I would hunt for the latest revision of a drawing across five email threads. I would find two versions and realize neither was the final one.

I spent an hour asking engineering to clarify a spec that should have been on the drawing. I spent thirty minutes attaching files only to realize I forgot the test requirements.

I had calls with vendors where I spent forty-five minutes explaining a BOM because it contradicted the drawing.

I learned this the hard way. None of those hours were sourcing. They were clerical work I had offloaded to myself.

The fix was discipline. I started organizing the package once. I wrote everything down before sending.

You can run the same audit on your own RFQs. It takes 15 minutes.

How many hours did you spend chasing your own RFQ package before it ever left your desk?
